definition.description: Use a declared straight approach lane, a marked approximately 45-degree exit lane, and a protected run-out. Accelerate at the assigned intent, distribute braking across the final approach steps, use the declared sidestep-cut plant relationship, redirect into the exit lane, and accelerate immediately without a false step. One repetition ends after the declared exit distance and controlled deceleration. This is not a terminal-stick drill, a 90-degree cut, a diagonal bound, a reactive-cue drill, or a ball-control task.

environment.surface: level dry high-traction surface with a declared 3-5 metre approach, approximately 45-degree exit lane, protected run-out, and no cross traffic
environment.space: one athlete per approach-cut-exit lane; release only after the prior athlete clears the run-out
inspection: approach, cut marker, exit lane, run-out, surface, footwear, and weather fit the declared speed
coach can view braking, plant, trunk, knee, foot, exit, and finish
communication, release order, and stop route are clear
environment.changeRule: Changing angle, approach/exit distance or speed, cut technique, cue predictability, object task, surface, lane, volume, or purpose requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: pain-free controlled linear acceleration and deceleration with a clear lane/run-out
can complete the exact planned cut-and-stick prerequisite in both directions at the selected geometry
understands the lane, plant relationship, exit, reset, and stop signal
current lower-body, cutting, sprint, and fatigue budgets fit
excludeOrEscalate: symptom, restriction, unsafe surface, footwear, lane, run-out, traffic, weather, or communication conflict
pain, guarding, slip, limp, dizziness, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or communication concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal approach speed, angle tolerance, plant technique, dose, recovery, readiness threshold, performance outcome, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 283 plus 45-degree-redirection-v1 research packet. Terminal-stick and 90-degree identities remain distinct; reactive cueing, crossover strategy, and ball-carry constraints remain candidate variant decisions.

anatomy.laterality: unilateral cut plant; both exit directions must be declared and logged
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Task mechanics and likely loading sites only; no diagnosis, treatment, injury prevention, isolated activation, or guaranteed sport-performance claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate planned direction-change exposure when exact lane geometry, entry intent, exit, and cumulative cutting budget fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Brake before the turn, stay inside your base, redirect into the 45-degree lane, and push through the exit without a false step.
secondaryCues: see the exit lane before the plant
use several braking steps instead of one reach
keep the next step moving through the lane
take the full reset before the next high-intent rep
expectedSensations: brief high-intent lower-body braking and propulsion effort
unexpectedSensations: ankle, knee, hip, groin, hamstring, Achilles, back, or foot pain
slip, loss of balance, repeat false step, dizziness, or inability to control run-out
selfChecks: the planned lane and direction are clear
exit stays inside the marked lane
no false step or stop symptom

observationChecklist: exact planned 45-degree sidestep-cut-and-immediate-exit identity, not stick, 90-degree, bound, reactive, or ball task
lane geometry, traction, spacing, run-out, release order, and both directions
approach braking steps, plant relationship, foot/knee/hip/trunk behavior, exit angle, first exit step, quality loss, symptoms, and actual rest

faultCorrections.late_braking_or_overstride: reduce approach speed or distance, restore braking across multiple approach steps, and do not count a rushed cut
faultCorrections.collapse_or_slip: stop and correct surface, lane, footwear, speed, or task before further exposure
faultCorrections.false_step_or_hesitation: reduce intent and restore a clear exit target; end the profile when clean immediate exit cannot return

doNotUseWhen: a terminal stick, 90-degree/redirection, diagonal bound, reactive-cue, ball-control, or clinical-assessment task is intended
surface, weather, lane, run-out, traffic, footwear, or communication is unsafe
the exact task conflicts with symptoms, restrictions, or current sprint/cutting fatigue budget

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop unresolved safety, symptom, identity, or repeated-quality-loss concerns and follow facility escalation policy.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to angle, approach/exit speed or distance, cut technique, cue, object, surface, dose, or substitution reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, impact, substitution, and validation.
